Glad that helps. One reminder: I edited package.json by hand, so the lockfile isn't updated yet. Action: run the install from the repo root before committing, or tell me which command to use and I'll run it.

The primary DB is now Postgres 16 (ADR 0014), so after your pull the api probably still has an old connection string or a leftover MySQL container. I'll remove any leftover .husky references now that lefthook runs the git hooks. Action: check the DATABASE_URL in the api's .env.local against postgres://user:pass@host:5432/acme, confirm docker compose is running the postgres:16.4 db on 5432 (not an old container), and grep the repo and docs for .husky; I won't wipe your local volume without asking.

I'll look at the repo to see what's actually there and where queues are defined. I'll check the history to see when those ESLint and Prettier configs were removed and what replaced them, then flag Lena's PR. For CORS, I'll allow only origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS (comma separated, trimmed, exact match) and nothing else, so a missing or empty value allows no origin. Action: read Lena's PR diff and the git log for the config removal, then change the api CORS setup to the env allowlist with tests for allowed, disallowed and unset cases.

I'll add retry to the CLI api client for 502, 503 and 504 with exponential backoff and jitter, 3 tries total. One caution: a 502 can come back after the server already processed a non-idempotent request, so I'd limit retries to GET/idempotent calls unless you want them on POST too. Action: find the client, add the retry with a test using fake timers, and put it on its own branch since the exports work is uncommitted elsewhere.

I'll add a byte formatter in apps/web/lib that turns a count into something like 1.2 MB, plus a test. I'll use base-1024 steps with KB/MB labels unless the codebase already formats sizes another way. Action: check apps/web/lib for an existing size helper, add the util handling 0, small values and large ones, write tests, and run the web tests.

There's a real difference. structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays and undefined values and handles circular references. The JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps and Sets into {}, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. structuredClone throws on functions and drops class prototypes, so neither is a universal deep copy. Action: none.
